title: Why you got fewer IPO shares

scenes.head: You applied for 10,000 shares. You got 2,000.
scenes.line: Eh, have a seat and let's have our money talk, quickly. You applied for 10,000 shares in a new offer, and you only got 2,000. Did somebody cheat you? Patience now! We go get there.
scenes.img: A confused young Nigerian man looking at a letter in his hands, sitting on a bed, soft morning light

scenes.head: What is an IPO?
scenes.body: Initial Public Offering: a company sells shares to the public for the first time
scenes.line: An Initial Public Offering, or IPO, is when a company sells its shares to the public for the first time, at a fixed offer price, for a set period.
scenes.img: A modern Nigerian company headquarters building with a crowd of people outside, celebration mood, no logos

scenes.head: Oversubscribed
scenes.body: People asked for more shares than were on offer
scenes.line: Now, if people ask for more shares than the company is selling, the offer is oversubscribed. So, the shares are shared out using a formula called the basis of allotment, and many people get fewer than they asked for.
scenes.img: A long queue of Nigerian people outside an office building, many holding forms, busy day

scenes.head: Your extra money comes back
scenes.body: Returned for the shares you didn't get
scenes.line: The money for the shares you didn't get is returned to you. Make sure your bank details and Bank Verification Number are correct, so it comes back without wahala.
scenes.img: Nigerian naira notes being handed back across a desk, close-up of hands, warm light

scenes.head: Then the shares land in your CSCS account
scenes.body: After the allotment is approved, trading can start
scenes.line: Once the allotment is approved, your shares are credited to your Central Securities Clearing System account, and then the shares can start trading on the exchange.
scenes.img: A Nigerian woman checking her investment account on a laptop, satisfied, modern apartment

scenes.head: A hot IPO is not guaranteed profit
scenes.body: Read the prospectus. Understand the business first.
scenes.line: One more thing. A popular offer is not a guarantee of profit. Read the prospectus, and understand the business before you apply.
scenes.img: A thick prospectus document on a desk next to reading glasses and a cup of tea, natural light
